rationale: The answer rests on the alternative-cost machinery: as part of casting any spell the caster announces intent to pay an alternative cost (601.2b/118.9/118.9a), and Archive Trap's alternative-cost ability functions on the stack no matter which zone it was cast from (113.6d), so Mission Briefing's permission to cast from the graveyard doesn't restrict it. Groups because one cost rule plus the zone-of-function rule are both load-bearing.

Two-Headed Giant teams are two individual players (810.1) whose resources aren't shared and whose damage/life events happen to each player individually before hitting the shared total (810.5, 810.9); any of these establishes that teammates are separate, independently targetable players.

Two facts: drawing from an empty library means no card is drawn and the player loses the game the next time anyone would get priority (104.3c, which 704.5b restates as the state-based action), and an ability triggers only if its trigger event actually happens, so nothing is revealed and neither Keranos trigger triggers (603.2g).

Resolution order is last-in-first-out (117.7/608.1), Veil of Summer's hexproof from blue and black makes Nico an illegal target for the blue Telemin Performance (702.11d), and a spell whose only target is illegal on resolution is removed from the stack without resolving (608.2b).

Flash would normally let Nicholas cast The Wandering Emperor at instant speed (702.8a, with 117.1a defining sorcery-speed timing), but Teferi's restriction that opponents cast only when they could cast a sorcery beats the permission (101.2), so the scenario can't happen.
Both chunks state the Two-Headed Giant starting life total of 30; either one answers the question, so they're alternatives.

A card cast for its morph cost is a 2/2 face-down creature spell with no mana cost (702.37a/702.37c, restated by 708.2a), and an object with no mana cost has mana value 0 (202.3a). Both halves are needed to reach 'mana value 0'.
There are exactly five colors and colorless is the absence of color (105.1, 105.2, 105.2c); any of these states that colorless isn't a color Alexis could choose.

The Glaive's static ability grants vigilance and menace unconditionally in layer 6 (613.1f, 604.1) while only the power boost is the Gate-dependent layer 7c modification (613.4c); the question is mostly card reading, so any of these continuous-effect chunks is the best available support.

Tandem Takedown uses the word 'target' once for the damaged creature, and a single instance of 'target' picks exactly one object (115.3, restated in 601.2c), so both Devoted Heroes hit the same creature.

The number of creature cards in the graveyard is information the ability needs, and that information is determined once, when the ability resolves (608.2h) - by then the graveyard is empty, so zero tokens.

Piracy restricts what the mana may be spent on but that's only a restriction on spending (106.6), and unspent mana simply sits in the pool and empties at end of step or phase (106.4) - both are needed to say Atlas may tap and spend nothing.

Essence Feed's instructions happen in the order written, so the tokens exist before the life gain (608.2c); the Heliod trigger goes on the stack only the next time a player would get priority, i.e. after the spell finishes resolving (603.3/117.5); and a triggered ability's targets are chosen when it's put on the stack (603.3d/115.1d), by which point the tokens are legal targets.

The CR has no rule defining 'another', so the closest citable basis is the targeting rule that otherwise would have let the same creature be chosen for both instances of 'target' (115.3/601.2c); the word 'another' overrides that in plain English.

The answer turns on who puts the poison counters on: infect damage causes the source's controller (Alejandro, who controls Vorinclex) to give the counters (702.90b/120.3b), which is why they're doubled. The judge also cited the toxic analogue, so 702.164c/120.3g are kept as alternatives stating the same 'source's controller gives the counters' fact.

Abrupt Decay's 'can't be countered' ability functions on the stack and beats Arcane Denial's attempt to counter it (113.6g/101.2), Arcane Denial still does as much as it can (609.3) so its draw clauses apply, and those draws are delayed triggered abilities that happen at the next upkeep (603.7a).

Dearly Departed's counter-granting ability is one that states it functions from the graveyard (113.6b), but Yixlid Jailer's ability-removing effect applies in layer 6 and strips it while it's there (613.1f/113.10), so Fugitive Wizard enters with no counter.

Skullcrack makes the damage unpreventable, and unpreventable damage still gets dealt even though prevention shields are applied and do nothing (615.12); 101.2's 'can't beats can' states the same outcome more generally.

Mana value is the total mana in the mana cost (202.3), and while the spell is on the stack each X equals the announced value (202.3e/107.3a), so Hangarback Walker with X=3 has mana value 6 and dodges Thoughtbind.

Sram's Expertise's instructions resolve in the order written so the tokens exist before the free cast (608.2c); escalate is an additional cost (702.120a); and additional costs still apply, and are announced, when a spell is cast for an alternative cost such as 'without paying its mana cost' during resolution (118.9d/601.2b/608.2g).

Mindcrank can trigger mid-resolution, but the trigger waits and goes on the stack the next time a player would receive priority, i.e. after Vampiric Tutor finishes resolving (117.2a, 603.3, 117.5 all state this); by then the tutored card is on top of the library and gets milled.

The draw is a turn-based action at the start of the draw step (504.1) and the active player only then gets priority (504.2); both are needed to place Nicole's instant window after the draw but before any sorcery.

Knowledge Exploitation is a Kindred sorcery whose Kindred subtypes are creature types (308.2), so it really is a Rogue spell and Frogtosser Banneret's reduction applies; 308.1 is the companion chunk in the same section.

Surge of Salvation makes Norah an illegal choice for 'target opponent' (702.11c/702.11d), and a triggered ability with no legal choices for a required target is simply removed from the stack, so none of it happens - including the draw and lifegain (603.3d).

Adelynn may announce any value of X when activating (107.3a/601.2b), but on resolution the 'up to' choice can't be made illegally and the ability's own 'can't cause more than seven' clause caps it, so it does only as much as possible (608.2d/609.3/101.2) - six counters.

Ajani's ability uses the exiled creature's last known information for its power, so Naomi gains 6 (608.2h); at 13 life the surviving Death's Shadow has 0 toughness and is put into the graveyard (704.5f); and that check happens before Angelo would next get priority (704.3/117.5).

An effect that refers to controlling a commander means any permanent on the battlefield that is a commander, not specifically your own (903.3d); 903.3 states that being a commander is an attribute of the card itself, which supports the same reading.

Hexproof only stops the permanent from being the target of opponents' spells and abilities (702.11b), and being affected by a spell that never says 'target' isn't targeting (115.10a/115.10), so Flesh Duplicate can copy Hollowhenge Huntmaster.

The trigger still resolves after Shaman of the Pack dies because it exists on the stack independently of its source (113.7a), and the Elf count is determined when the ability resolves (608.2h) - at which point Ada controls none, so zero life lost.
Both chunks state the Commander starting life total of 40; either one answers the question.

Curtain of Light makes the creature a blocked creature even though no creature blocks it (509.1h, restated in the Blocked Creature glossary entry), but an ability that triggers on becoming blocked by a creature doesn't trigger when an effect does the blocking (509.3d).

Rest in Peace and Dauthi Voidwalker are two replacement effects competing over Lightning Bolt hitting the graveyard, so its controller picks which applies (616.1/616.1e); separately, the Voidwalker has lethal damage marked and is destroyed as a state-based action (704.5g) before being exiled.
103.5 is the whole mulligan procedure and states outright that once a player chooses not to take a mulligan, that hand is their opening hand and they may take no further mulligans.

Putting a resolving sorcery into its owner's graveyard is the final part of its resolution (608.2n, with 608.2 stating that step is followed last), so Leyline of the Void is already destroyed and can't replace Aura Mutation's trip to the graveyard.

Elesh Norn makes the landfall ability trigger an additional time, and the game determines how many times it triggers rather than re-invoking itself (603.2d); each copy then checks on resolution how many times the ability has resolved this turn (608.2h), so the first gives life and the second gives mana.

Soul-Scar Mage turns the damage into -1/-1 counters, which annihilate the +1/+1 counters as a state-based action (704.5q, identically stated in 122.3), and adapt only checks that the creature has no +1/+1 counters when the ability resolves (701.46a), so it can adapt again.

Blood Moon sets Sacred Peaks's subtype to Mountain, so it loses its other land types (305.7), and Emeria Shepherd's ability checks whether the land is a Plains when the ability resolves (608.2h) - it isn't, so Garenbrig Carver goes to hand.

A split card is multicolored everywhere but the stack because its characteristics are its halves combined (709.4/709.4b), while on the stack only the half being cast exists (709.3b), so the Illusion spell is monocolored and General Ferrous Rokiric doesn't trigger.

When an effect lets a player cast the exiled adventurer card, the player still chooses whether to play it normally or as an Adventure (715.3), because the Adventure characteristics are alternative characteristics the object may use (715.2).

Escape is just an alternative cost, so the escaped card becomes an ordinary spell on the stack (702.138a), and a spell on the stack is a legal target for a counterspell, which removes it from the stack before it resolves (115.2/701.6a).

In the graveyard an adventurer card has only its normal (creature) characteristics (715.4), because the Adventure text is only alternative characteristics the object may have as a spell (715.2) - so Guardian Naga isn't an instant or sorcery card Flashback can target.

The legend rule applies to legendary permanents with the same name regardless of card type (704.5j, restated in the Legend Rule glossary entry), and it's checked as a state-based action as soon as the spell finishes resolving, before anyone gets priority (704.3/117.5).

A creature stays an attacking creature until it's removed from combat or the combat phase ends (508.1k, the Attacking Creature glossary entry, and 506.4 listing what removes a permanent from combat), so after damage it's still a legal target for Reconnaissance.

The activated ability goes on the stack and exists independently of Molten-Tail Masticore (602.2a/113.7a), and the player may activate mana abilities - sacrificing the Masticore to Thermopod - after that but before costs are paid (601.2g/601.2h), so it's in the graveyard in time to be exiled for the cost.

The nonhybrid equivalent of each {2/B} is announced during casting (601.2b), a monocolored hybrid symbol can be paid with one black or two mana of any type (107.4e), and generic mana in costs can be paid with any type of mana including black (107.4b) - so six black mana is legal.

Blessed Hippogriff in the graveyard has only its creature characteristics (715.4, with 715.2 stating the Adventure characteristics apply only while it's a spell), so it isn't an instant or sorcery card Mission Briefing can choose.

Oubliette phases the creature out 'until' Oubliette leaves, and that phrasing creates a second one-shot effect that phases it in only when the stated event happens (610.4); the normal untap-step phase-in is part of the phasing keyword's rules modification (702.26a), which doesn't apply here.

The 'except its name is Lazav, Dimir Mastermind' clause is a copy effect that modifies a characteristic as part of the copying process, and the modified value becomes the copy's copiable value (707.9b, introduced by 707.9), so the name is Lazav, Dimir Mastermind.

In the graveyard a split card has the combined characteristics and every card type of both halves, so Road // Ruin is an instant card and a legal target (709.4/709.4c); and when it's cast the player simply chooses which half to cast, with nothing restricting the choice (709.3/709.3a).

Party size is calculated automatically by the game rather than declared by the player (700.8a), and when a creature could fill more than one slot it's counted to give the highest result (700.8b), so Alvaro can't choose a smaller reduction.
